summary:
Iter 18 - Task B (AI Yoga library + guided session detail). BACKEND: 17/17 tests PASS in test_iter18_ai_yoga.py. All acceptance criteria met - GET /api/yoga/library (401 without auth; returns items/categories/levels/recommended/dosha/total; exactly 8 sessions across Morning/Therapy/Women/Sleep/Detox/Cooling/Quick/Breath; each item has thumbnail/duration_min/dosha_target/instructor/level/premium=false), category filter (?category=Morning) returns only that category, dosha filter (?dosha=Vata) returns items whose dosha_target contains 'Vata', invalid category returns empty items but still 200. For patient1 (saved Prakriti = Vata from iter17), `dosha` in response is 'Vata' and `recommended` returns 5 items whose dosha_target includes Vata (<=6 as spec). For doctor role, `dosha` is null and `recommended` is empty. GET /api/yoga/sessions/{id} returns full payload with poses[] (name/duration_sec/cue) and youtube_id; unknown id -> 404. POST /api/yoga/log persists to `yoga_sessions` with logged_at (Mongo _id excluded from response); unknown session_id -> 404; missing session_id -> 422. GET /api/yoga/mine on a fresh_patient returns zeros; after a single 300s log, total_minutes=5, streak_days=1, total_sessions=1.

FRONTEND: patient1@vaidhyaji.example.com logged in via /auth/login. Absolute nav to /ai-yoga works (previously tested /home/ai-yoga which is unmatched - that was a test-script bug, not a product bug). Hero renders. Stats pills (yg-back present) show '1 DAY STREAK / 5 MINUTES / 1 SESSIONS' (persisted from backend test). 'For your Prakriti - Vata / Recommended for you' row visible with 5 yg-rec-* cards. All 9 category chips (yg-cat-All + 8 categories) present. All 8 item cards (yg-item-*) rendered. Tapping 'Morning' chip filters live to 1 item (yg-item-morning-energy-20). Tapping item navigates to /yoga/morning-energy-20. Session detail: YouTube iframe renders on web, timer card shows 'POSE 1 OF 15' with pose name 'Centering breath' and cue, ys-play/ys-prev/ys-next/ys-finish/ys-back all present. Play -> ys-pause appears; pause -> ys-play returns. Skip next: POSE 1 -> 2 correctly. Tap ys-pose-3 jumps to POSE 4 OF 15. ys-finish shows web alert (auto-accepted), POST /yoga/log fires, and router.back() returns to /ai-yoga. No red screens, no runtime errors.

Deprecated packages / RN issues detected: same 3 pre-existing web dev warnings as prior iterations (react-native-web shadow*, Image resizeMode, expo-notifications web listener) - no new deprecations. `expo-av` is NOT used in the new yoga screens (uses YouTube iframe on web + react-native-webview on native, which is correct).

minor.issue: `recommended` is sliced from all items filtered by dominant dosha, but if a `category=X` filter is passed the `recommended` block is still computed and returned - however server.py:2718 correctly guards `if saved_dosha and not dosha` (skips only when dosha filter set). So passing `?category=Sleep` still returns full-library recommended, which is intentional. Note: on the frontend, the recommended row is not re-fetched when a category chip is tapped because the client passes `category` but not `dosha` - so recommended stays constant across category filtering. This matches the spec but worth documenting.

`saved_dosha` uses .split('-')[0] to take the dominant of hyphenated dosha strings (e.g. 'Vata-Pitta' -> 'Vata'). Consistent with iter17 note that /prakriti/assess stores hyphenated dosha. Works, but if a future scoring change flips ordering the dominant token could shift; consider persisting a separate dominant_dosha field.

issues: Stats pills eyebrow uses letter-spacing:1 + text-transform:uppercase on a small 10px label. Legible but at the edge of contrast on the brand background - fine for mobile but may want +1px.

react_native_issues.issue: 'shadow*' style props are deprecated. Use 'boxShadow'. Reference: pre-existing across app (not introduced by yoga screens).
'Image: style.resizeMode is deprecated. Please use props.resizeMode.' Pre-existing; not from new yoga code.
'Listening to push token changes is not yet fully supported on web.' Expected on web preview, no impact on native.
'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents.' Pre-existing (from login screen), not new.

critical_code_review_comments: yoga/[id].tsx:58-82 - timer useEffect closure recomputes on `running`/`session` change but not on poseIdx. Because setPoseIdx is called inside setRemaining callback with a setTimeout(..., 0), the setTimeout runs before the next interval tick and sets remaining to the next pose's duration. Works but is fragile - safer pattern is a single useEffect that reads latest poseIdx via a ref. If the interval fires between the setPoseIdx and the setTimeout it could double-tick. Recommend refactoring to a single reducer + useRef(intervalRef) with a proper cleanup that reads the latest state via ref.

yoga/[id].tsx:85 - `isSessionDone = poseIdx === poses.length - 1 && remaining === 0 && elapsed > 0 && !running`. On natural completion, `running` is set to false inside the interval callback, but the guard `remaining === 0` requires the next tick to hit. It works but the derived-boolean approach has an off-by-one - if the user pauses on the last pose with remaining>0, `isSessionDone` is false so the 'Log & exit' label doesn't show. Minor UX only.

yoga/[id].tsx:87-102 - auto-log useEffect could fire twice under React 18 StrictMode; the `logged` flag guards against duplicates but the request has already been queued. Consider using a ref to track in-flight requests too.

yoga/[id].tsx:294 - onPress on ys-pose-{i} pauses the timer AND jumps to that pose. Good UX. However `elapsed` is NOT reset on jump, so if a user jumps forward from pose 1 to pose 5, elapsed still reflects only the ticked seconds. When they finish, `completed_seconds` will underreport the actual time in the session. Acceptable trade-off (logs what was actually done, not what was watched).
server.py:2719 - `_yoga_by_id` is called inside the recommended-list comprehension for every summary. O(n*m). Not a perf issue at 8 items, but if the library grows to 50+, pre-index by id.

server.py:2785 - streak calculation: `days` is sorted DESC and iterated with `expected = now - timedelta(days=i)`. Correct. If a user logs at 23:59 UTC on day X and then at 00:05 UTC on day X+2, streak resets to 1 - as expected. Good.

ai-yoga.tsx:27 - `api.yogaLibrary({ category: cat === 'All' ? undefined : cat })` re-fetches on every chip change. Fine, but this also re-computes the `recommended` row on the server (server always builds recommended for patient with saved dosha, regardless of category). Could add a client-side cache keyed by cat for snappier UX; not blocking.

success_rate.frontend: 100% - all testIDs present, timer play/pause/next/prev/jump/finish all verified

seed_data_creation: test_iter18_ai_yoga.py registered 1 ephemeral fresh_patient (email prefix TEST_) per pytest session. Wrote 1 yoga_sessions row for patient1 (quick-desk-10, 300s completed) and 1 for fresh_patient (pranayama-basics-15, 300s). The frontend ys-finish additionally wrote 1 more row for patient1 (morning-energy-20, brief elapsed) during UI verification. Total: 3 yoga_sessions entries added, all attributable via user_id.
context_for_next_testing_agent: AI Yoga Task B complete. Frontend route is /ai-yoga (NOT /home/ai-yoga - Expo Router serves it at the root and the 'home' segment is a tab group but ai-yoga is a top-level route). Session detail is /yoga/[id]. All timer controls: ys-play/ys-pause/ys-prev/ys-next/ys-finish/ys-back/ys-pose-{i}. Backend endpoints all live: /api/yoga/library, /api/yoga/sessions/{id}, /api/yoga/log, /api/yoga/mine. patient1@vaidhyaji.example.com already has Vata prakriti saved from iter17 and now has 2-3 yoga_sessions logged from this iter18 testing (streak_days=1, total_minutes reflects only the 300s log because ys-finish elapsed was tiny). For a clean streak=0 test, use a freshly-registered patient. rca_of_issue: Not applicable - Task B completed cleanly with zero critical bugs and zero minor blockers. The two 'minor' backend notes are documentation-level, and the code review comments are refactor suggestions (timer effect coupling, off-by-one in isSessionDone, potential StrictMode double-fetch) - none are functional bugs today.
